clue.text: See 9
Cut head and face

parts.note: the top of something is its head
a side is a face, as of a cube or a mountain

explanation.surface: An instruction to slash someone's head and face, like a grisly order.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef taken from the hindquarter, one of the butcher's cuts.

clue.text: Pin to act on short spring

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A pin that is meant to work on a coiled spring, as in some mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden peg used to join pieces of wood, a kind of pin.

clue.text: Shelter in trees by banks of elm with one bending over

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so the outside letters of elm

parts.note: a bower is one who bows, someone bending over

explanation.surface: Someone taking cover under trees beside the elms, with a figure stooping over them.
explanation.definitionFit: To embower is to enclose in a bower, a leafy shady retreat among trees.

clue.text: Dwarf runs into Sleepy, essentially outside

indicators.note: into says the runs piece goes inside
outside says the core of Sleepy wraps round the other piece
the essence or core of the word, so its central letters

parts.note: the middle two letters of the six-letter name
clips means runs or moves fast, as in going at a clip

explanation.surface: A Snow White dwarf bumps into his companion Sleepy, out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwarf' and 'Sleepy' suggest the Seven Dwarfs, but Dwarf is a verb meaning to overshadow, and runs means moves at a clip.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to overshadow it or make it seem small by comparison.

clue.text: Tory party member getting protection

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative, abbreviated CON
a do is a party
M is an abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A Conservative Party member gains security, perhaps a bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A condom is a contraceptive sheath, often simply called protection.

clue.text: Tidy up room initially left in big mess

indicators.note: tidying up rearranges things, so these letters are reordered
the first letters of left and in

parts.note: first letter gives L
first letter gives I

explanation.surface: An instruction to clean a bedroom that was first left in a terrible state.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, complicated situation, a tangle or mess.

clue.text: Did substitute put feet up on training day?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the next
in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: paws are animal feet
PE is physical education, training

explanation.surface: A footballer on the bench relaxes during a training day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did substitute' suggests a footballer coming on as a sub, but it is a past-tense verb meaning exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To have swapped is to have exchanged one thing for another, a synonym.

clue.text: Flirt without fellow? Ms Denise Van Outen dancing around subject

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters around into a new order
without means the letter for fellow is removed from flirt

explanation.surface: The TV presenter Denise Van Outen dances round a partner, flirting, with no man in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing F from FLIRT leaves LIRT; with MS DENISE VAN OUTEN, those letters rearrange into the two-word answer. Denise Van Outen is a British TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Environmental studies is an academic discipline, a subject taught in schools and universities.

clue.text: Bring up leader of school form

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a form is a long bench, as is a pew

explanation.surface: Raising the matter of a head boy or girl in a school class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' here means a bench, not a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, a coarse sense of bringing food back up.

clue.text: All hands below deck on this? Cheers round bar: one sailor returning

definitions.text: All hands below deck on this?

indicators.note: returning means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, cheers
a round thing is O
to ban is to bar
an means one
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A ship's crew drinks toasts in the bar below deck, then a sailor goes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All hands' suggests the whole crew, but here it means bunches of bananas, which are called hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana boat is a cargo ship carrying bananas, whose bunches are known as hands, in its hold.

clue.text: One on bed with tablet: that hurts

parts.note: a pill is a tablet
ow is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: A patient lying in bed takes medication and complains of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a cushion that rests at the head of a bed.

clue.text: Is old hotel on seafront rejected? It's very like another one

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a prom (promenade) is a seafront walk

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an old seaside hotel has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: A prom is the British word for a seaside promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: An isomorph is a substance or organism with the same form or crystal structure as another.

clue.text: Season with this football manager getting a trophy

parts.note: Pep Guardiola is the Manchester City manager
per means a, as in 'five pounds a head'
a pot is slang for a sports trophy

explanation.surface: A football manager wins silverware in this season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a sporting season, but it is the verb meaning to flavour food.
explanation.definitionFit: A pepper pot is a shaker used to sprinkle ground pepper over food as seasoning.

clue.text: Fat swelling under pressure point

indicators.note: in a down clue, the swelling comes below the pressure

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a lump is a swelling
a ness is a headland or point, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A swelling on the body made worse by pressing on a sore point.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumpness is roundness of body, a mild word for fatness, both nouns.

clue.text: Smoothly pass down wing, keeping inside line

indicators.note: keeping inside means the wing holds the line within it

parts.note: a side, as of a building, is a wing

explanation.surface: A winger runs along the flank, staying just inside the touchline.
explanation.definitionFit: To slide is to glide down a surface with a smooth, continuous motion.

clue.text: American to fight roughly

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: An American squares up to brawl in a rough way.
explanation.definitionFit: About means approximately, as in 'about ten people', an adverb synonym.

clue.text: See 19
Previous issues of Eagle go: obtain mag in jumble

indicators.note: a jumble is a disordered heap, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Back numbers of the Eagle comic, found in a jumble sale, must go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previous issues' looks like back numbers of a magazine, but it means psychological problems from the past. The Eagle was a British boys' comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional baggage is an idiom for unresolved feelings and problems carried over from past experience.

clue.text: Bigger hospital getting heart bypass?

indicators.note: a bypass goes round something, so the heart goes around the hospital letter

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A larger hospital wins funding for heart bypass operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Thicker means wider or more massive, so larger in girth, a comparative synonym.

clue.text: Fan and ventilator to tackle damp, occasionally

indicators.note: tackling something means getting to grips with it, so the airer holds the other letters

parts.note: an airer is something that airs, a ventilator

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters, every other one

parts.note: alternate letters give DM

explanation.surface: A fan and a ventilator are brought in to deal with a damp problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like another airing device beside ventilator, but it means an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiastic follower, so an admirer, a synonym.

clue.text: Reject plant that's in row

indicators.note: that's in says the plant word sits inside the row word

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise
to sow is to plant

explanation.surface: A gardener throws out a plant that is growing in the row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line of plants, but it is a noisy row.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge someone, to cast them off.

clue.text: Tip: any horse at the finish struggles over Grand National

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: struggles suggests thrashing about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A betting tip: any horse struggling at the finish of the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase. 'National' here is a noun, a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian is a citizen of Egypt, so a national of that country.

clue.text: Returns home: needs to move nearer

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to come is to move nearer

explanation.surface: Someone who comes home needs to move closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for financial yields.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns on money are earnings or revenue, which is what income means.

clue.text: Patients' chests?

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like patients' chests on a ward, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors call the people they treat cases, and the same word names packing boxes or crates.

clue.text: Find attractive model: pose and dress down

parts.note: to take to someone is to find them attractive
T as in the Model T Ford
to pose a question is to ask

explanation.surface: A photographer is drawn to a model and asks her to pose and get dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress down' looks like wearing casual clothes, but it means to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone down is to reprimand them severely, an idiom with the same meaning.

clue.text: Type character at end of script

wordplay.reading: S, the first, or T, the last, of script

parts.note: script has two ends, so the character at an end is either its first letter or its last, and the phrase spells out that choice

explanation.surface: A typed letter placed at the end of a written script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character at end of script' can be S or T, as script has two ends; spelt out, S OR T is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a type or kind, as in 'what sort of person'.

clue.text: Refraining from relaxing on cocaine

indicators.note: in an across clue, on puts relaxing after the cocaine letter

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine
easing means relaxing, loosening

explanation.surface: Someone stops taking drugs, or relaxes while high on cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceasing is stopping an action, which is refraining from continuing it.

clue.text: Taking out date that's confident

parts.note: an era is a period or date
sure means confident

explanation.surface: Taking someone out on a date with a self-assured air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking out' looks like going on a date, but it means removal.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is the act of rubbing something out, deleting it.
